title: Discourse & Argumentation
description: Engage with the highest levels of rhetorical sophistication in English: understanding discourse structure, analysing argumentative strategies, recognising logical fallacies, and constructing linguistically dense, rhetorically effective arguments. For C2 learners who want to write, speak, and think in English at a near-native level.

content.content: {"time":1700130001000,"blocks":[{"id":"dA1bB2cC3d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Discourse analysis examines how language above the sentence level creates meaning. A coherent text achieves unity at two levels: the macro (overall structure and argument progression) and the micro (sentence-level cohesion)."}},{"id":"dD4eE5fF6g","type":"header","data":{"text":"Micro-Level Cohesive Devices","level":3}},{"id":"dG7hH8iI9j","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Reference: pronouns and demonstratives pointing back to earlier items (this, the former, the latter)","Substitution: replacing a phrase with a shorter form ('She applied for the job. So did he.')","Ellipsis: omitting a recoverable element ('Can you come?' 'I can.')","Conjunction: additive (moreover, furthermore), adversative (nevertheless, yet), causal (consequently, thereby), temporal (subsequently, hitherto)","Lexical cohesion: reiteration (repetition, synonym, superordinate, near-synonym) and collocation"]}},{"id":"dJ0kK1lL2m","type":"header","data":{"text":"Macro-Level Discourse Structures","level":3}},{"id":"dM3nN4oO5p","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Problem–Solution: situation → problem → solution → evaluation","Claim–Evidence–Warrant: the Toulmin model of argument","Narrative: orientation → complication → resolution → coda","Compare–Contrast: block method vs. point-by-point"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

pairs.right: Using 'this', 'it', 'the former' to point back to previous content
Omitting words that can be recovered from context
Using synonyms, near-synonyms, or superordinates to link ideas

questions.text: Which of the following demonstrates 'ellipsis' as a cohesive device?
options: She left and he left too.
She left because he asked her to.

questions.text: In the Toulmin model, what is the 'warrant'?
options: The logical principle connecting evidence to claim

content.content: {"time":1700130002000,"blocks":[{"id":"rA1bB2cC3d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Aristotle identified three primary modes of persuasion, which remain foundational to rhetoric and argumentation theory: ethos, pathos, and logos."}},{"id":"rD4eE5fF6g","type":"header","data":{"text":"The Three Appeals","level":3}},{"id":"rG7hH8iI9j","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Ethos (credibility) — The speaker/writer establishes authority and trustworthiness. Techniques: credentials, track record, consistent values, acknowledgement of limitations.","Pathos (emotion) — The argument appeals to the audience's emotions, values, and imagination. Techniques: vivid narrative, anecdote, emotive diction, metaphor.","Logos (logic) — The argument proceeds through reasoning and evidence. Techniques: statistics, case studies, analogy, syllogism, inductive/deductive reasoning."]}},{"id":"rJ0kK1lL2m","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Note: Sophisticated arguments integrate all three. Over-reliance on pathos without logos is emotionally manipulative; over-reliance on logos without pathos can fail to engage the audience. Ethos underpins the credibility of both."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

questions.text: A politician opens her speech: 'As a former nurse who worked through the pandemic, I know first-hand the pressures our NHS faces.' Which appeal is this primarily?
An advertisement shows a starving child and asks you to donate to a charity. Which appeal dominates?

content.content: {"time":1700130003000,"blocks":[{"id":"lfA1bB2cC3d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A logical fallacy is an error in reasoning that makes an argument unsound. Recognising fallacies is essential for both critical reading and the construction of valid arguments."}},{"id":"lfD4eE5fF6g","type":"header","data":{"text":"Key Fallacies","level":3}},{"id":"lfG7hH8iI9j","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Ad hominem — attacking the person rather than the argument ('You can't trust his climate research; he owns a car.')","Straw man — misrepresenting an opponent's argument to make it easier to attack","False dichotomy — presenting only two options when others exist ('Either you support this policy or you don't care about children.')","Slippery slope — claiming that one event will inevitably lead to extreme consequences without justification","Appeal to authority — citing an authority figure in an irrelevant field","Post hoc ergo propter hoc — assuming that because B followed A, A caused B"]}},{"id":"lfJ0kK1lL2m","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Refuting a fallacy: Name it, explain why the reasoning is invalid, then redirect to the substantive evidence."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

pairs.right: Attacking the speaker's character instead of the argument
Misrepresenting an opponent's position to defeat it easily
Presenting only two options when more exist
Claiming a small step inevitably leads to extreme consequences
Assuming that sequence in time means causation

lessons.title: Argument Density and Academic Register at C2

content.content: {"time":1700130004000,"blocks":[{"id":"adA1bB2cC3d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"C2 academic writing is characterised by high argument density: each sentence contributes meaningfully to the overall argument, with minimal padding. This requires mastery of nominalisation, complex syntax, and precise logical connectors."}},{"id":"adD4eE5fF6g","type":"header","data":{"text":"Nominalisation","level":3}},{"id":"adG7hH8iI9j","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Nominalisation converts verbs and adjectives into nouns, making writing more abstract and formal:"}},{"id":"adH1iI2jJ3k","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["We discovered X → Our discovery of X","The economy improved → The improvement in the economy","They failed to implement the policy → Their failure to implement the policy"]}},{"id":"adJ0kK1lL2m","type":"header","data":{"text":"Advanced Logical Connectors","level":3}},{"id":"adM3nN4oO5p","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["notwithstanding — despite what has been said/done (formal)","by virtue of — because of / owing to","insofar as — to the extent that","inasmuch as — since / to the degree that","predicated on — based on the assumption that","contingent upon — depending on"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: The success of the policy is ___ upon its implementation being consistent and well-funded. Notwithstanding ___ political opposition, the evidence suggests its effectiveness. The argument is ___ on the premise that behaviour change is possible at scale. Insofar ___ public trust is maintained, the reforms should proceed.

options: Converting verbs and adjectives into noun phrases
